requirements.requirement: Algorithm 1 applies to arbitrary nonempty input, not just a fixed example.
requirements.evidence: Research/Submission.lean:53-70 defines the actual numerical loop for any List ℝ and arbitrary add. algorithm1_spec (465-472) universally quantifies xs with xs ≠ [], proves the final stage is a singleton, and identifies its value with algorithm. final_tree (224-242) proves nonemptiness and singleton convergence rather than relying on headD defaults. algorithm_exact (479-488) proves the exact sum of the original list.

requirements.requirement: Exact offset pairing and simultaneous use of the old level.
requirements.evidence: roundValues (59-61) splits at (length+1)/2 and pairs corresponding entries of take/drop. roundValues_entry (92-105) proves the index rule and unavailable-partner branch. stagesValues_length (453-462) and stage_offset (447-450) connect current lengths/offsets to ceil(n/2^ℓ) and ceil(n/2^(ℓ+1)). IndependentChecks.lean proves symbolically for arbitrary f that the five-input root is f (f (f a d) c) (f b e), and the three-input root is f (f a c) b; these checks distinguish the intended schedule from adjacent pairing.
IndependentChecks.lean checks stagesValues at each of stages 0, 1, 2, 3 by unfolding the actual implementation and proving real arithmetic equalities. All checks compile. depth 5 = 3 is also checked.

requirements.requirement: Carried subtree is unchanged and incurs no extra rounding/addition call.
requirements.evidence: pair (30-33) returns the remaining list verbatim when either list is empty; pairValues (53-56) does the same without applying add. Tree.eval applies add only at node constructors (23-25). Independent symbolic checks prove round [a,b,c] = [node a c,b] and round [a,b,c,d,e] = [node a d,node b e,c] for arbitrary whole subtrees. Numerical symbolic checks retain the carried value c directly. The three-stage five-input root has exactly four applications of arbitrary f, with no artificial add-to-zero operation.

requirements.requirement: Input occurrences and multiplicities are preserved, including duplicates.
requirements.evidence: pair_leaves, round_leaves and stages_leaves (143-174) use List.Perm, which preserves multiplicities. algorithm_tree_spec (431-438) relates root leaves to the original list. theorem_3_1_list_local (377-388) transports List.Forall₂ along this permutation; theorem_3_1 (391-408) indexes perturbations by Fin xs.length, rather than a set of values. Independent check proves five copies of arbitrary x sum to 5*x under the actual schedule.

requirements.requirement: Singleton and odd-length inputs are covered.
requirements.evidence: Independent check proves algorithm f [x] = x for arbitrary f; depth 1 = 0 and no operation is required. Symbolic three- and five-input checks cover odd offsets and carry placement. General length and leaf permutation proofs do not assume even length or power-of-two size.

requirements.requirement: Depth is exactly ceil(log2 n), with at most this many additions on each leaf-to-root path.
requirements.evidence: depth (45) is Nat.clog 2 n. depth_spec (475-476) proves the characterization depth n ≤ k iff n ≤ 2^k. algorithm_tree_spec proves root height equals depth xs.length for all nonempty xs, using both the upper bound and leaves.length ≤ 2^height (419-428). stagesValues executes exactly depth stages. The error proof admits shorter carried paths and bounds them by the same depth.

requirements.requirement: Theorem 3.1 proves the componentwise gamma backward-error bound for the actual algorithm.
requirements.evidence: gamma (255) is d*u/(1-d*u). theorem_3_1 (391-408) states existence of Δ for every original index, algorithm add xs = Σ_i (xs.get i + Δ i), and |Δ i| ≤ gamma (depth xs.length) u * |xs.get i|. scale_error and gamma_step prove the bound, and tree_backward_error_local builds perturbed leaf occurrences inductively. algorithm_eq_tree connects this analysis to the numerical loop. Independent coordinatewise_check compiles for arbitrary coordinate type and component-specific operations; each coordinate has the same input length/depth. There is no replacement by a total forward-error bound or a larger linear-depth constant.

requirements.requirement: Rounding assumptions are local, noncircular, and nonvacuous.
requirements.evidence: ExecutionModel (293-294) requires only Tree.Valid at final trees. final_tree proves there is one such tree for every nonempty input. Tree.Valid (285-289) recursively requires the standard local relation add a b = (a+b)*(1+δ), |δ| ≤ u at executed nodes, without assuming a backward-error conclusion. Leaves require True because no arithmetic occurs there. Independent check proves exact addition satisfies RoundingModel for every u ≥ 0. The optional global corollary has a stronger global model, but the principal theorem uses only the run-local model.

requirements.requirement: No weakened substitute, proof placeholders, custom axioms, or missing imports.
requirements.evidence: Read all 490 source lines and the root module. Submission imports Mathlib; Research.lean imports Research.Submission. Source scan found no sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe/partial declarations. Independently reran lake env lean Research/Submission.lean: exit 0. #print axioms for theorem_3_1, algorithm1_spec, algorithm_exact reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no sorryAx or custom axioms. IndependentChecks.lean also compiles with exit 0. /evaluation/verification.json and verification.log report a successful build and no placeholders/custom axioms; these were corroborating evidence, not a semantic acceptance criterion.

assumptions_added.assessment: Standard nonnegativity implicit in unit roundoff; harmless, allows exact arithmetic u=0.

assumptions_added.assumption: Inputs and computed values are modeled by real numbers, with a pure deterministic binary operation satisfying the relative-error model on executed nodes.
assumptions_added.assessment: Standard abstraction of the source floating-point model and no overflow/underflow hypothesis. The theorem does not claim a verified concrete IEEE implementation. The global RoundingModel is stronger than run-local validity, but is needed only for an optional corollary.
Matches the requested nonempty scope and the use of ceil(log2 n); excludes only the unspecified empty reduction.

limitations: The candidate presents the theorem for scalar real lists. Componentwise use is obtained by applying it to each coordinate; an arbitrary-coordinate specialization was independently compiled under /output, rather than being a named vector theorem in the candidate.

No hardware floating-point implementation, overflow detector, physical parallel execution, or runtime call instrumentation is verified. Absence of extra arithmetic on carried subtrees is established from the expression structure and arbitrary-operation identities.
The review trusts the installed Lean 4.28.0 kernel and Mathlib dependencies, using standard axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Dependencies were not audited from first principles.
Concrete tests cover singleton, three/five-element odd lists, and five duplicate inputs; universal coverage rests on the inspected Lean proofs, not an exhaustive test enumeration.

An initial version of the reviewer-owned checks had proof elaboration/namespace errors; these were corrected only in /output. The final independent-checks.log records successful compilation and clean audited axiom dependencies. Candidate files were not edited.
